blockers.whatTheMechanismActuallyIs: byte_gate() reads `text = _SUBJECT_PATH.read_text()` and `raw = _SUBJECT_PATH.read_bytes()`, then compares `text == serialise(reconstruction)` and reports sha256 of `raw`. pathlib.Path.read_text() opens with newline=None, which is Python's universal-newline mode: '\r\n' and lone '\r' are both translated to '\n' before the comparator ever sees them. The equality that is tested is therefore over newline-normalised TEXT; the digest that is printed is over the real BYTES; and the two are different documents. parse_census() reads the same way, so the number-token census does not see it either.

blockers.whatThisIsAndIsNot: IT IS NOT A PAPER SEAL. JSON permits CR and CRLF only as inter-token whitespace, a raw control character inside a string is rejected by the host parser, and universal-newline translation touches nothing else, so the covert channel is roughly one trit per line of layout and carries no prose a reader would meet. I could not turn it into a payload and I say so. IT IS a demonstrated counterexample to the sentence the whole successor rests on, produced by exactly the edit shape B-VER12R-01 used — one file, artifact only, no checker access — and it is the reason this is BLOCKING rather than an observation: this lineage's standard, applied by the v11 and v12 reviewers to this record's predecessors, is that a load-bearing sentence falsified by experiment is a finding regardless of the size of the payload.
